book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_1:
The Epic of Kitay Bahsi
Wrath of the Skies and the Birth of Kiday

Long ago, a master who understood the language of fire and iron lived in the shadow of the mountains. His name was Kitay Bahsi.
book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_2:
He had forged many swords and crafted many suits of armor, yet he was satisfied with none of his works. Iron broke, gold bent, and even the strongest steel wore away with time.

Kitay Bahsi devoted his life to finding a metal superior to every ore.
book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_3:
One day, deep within the mountains, he found a pale ore he had never seen before. It resembled neither gold nor iron. The master melted it in his furnace, poured it into molds, and cooled it with water.

Yet there was something strange about the metal that emerged.
book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_4: When he struck it with his hammer, the metal trembled once more after the blow. When heated, it held its warmth for a long time; with every strike on the anvil, it seemed to learn the hammer's rhythm.
book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_5:
Kitay Bahsi realized that this ore was not merely strong: it remembered the force applied to it.

He forged nine works from the metal.
book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_6:
The first was a sword. When it struck an enemy, the echo of the first blow was felt a second time.

Then he made a pickaxe that could sense the vibrations of ores deep within stone.
book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_7: His axe found the cracks in a tree trunk, and his shovel cut through soil more easily with each stroke. His hoe awakened the life within the earth and brought abundance to crops.
book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_8:
The master forged four pieces of armor from the remaining metal.

His helmet revealed what lay beyond darkness, while his chestplate remembered the blows dealt against it.
book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_9: The armor covering his legs lightened his steps, and his boots carried the speed of the wind to his feet.
book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_10:
But the fame of these works did not spread only among humans.

The news reached Lei Gong, lord of thunder.
book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_11:
Lei Gong saw a mortal's ability to forge such powerful works as a challenge to his own might.

He darkened the sky, crashed the clouds together, and sent lightning that shook the mountains.
book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_12:
Kitay Bahsi did not abandon his forge.

When one of the bolts from the sky struck his anvil, the metal he had forged did not shatter.
book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_13:
Instead, it absorbed the lightning's force and continued to tremble upon the anvil.

Seeing this, Lei Gong separated fragments of his power and sent beings in his own image down to the earth.
book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_14:
Lightning burst from the hands of these beings, and electricity that struck one target leapt to another.

Kitay Bahsi took up the sword he had forged, donned his armor, and stood against them.
book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_15: With every blow, his sword struck a second time. His chestplate shook under every bolt, but the master remained standing.
book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_16:
At last, Lei Gong's avatars were defeated one by one.

But the god of thunder refused to accept his defeat.
book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_17:
He sent his avatars to lands where storms never ceased. From that day onward, rain did not stop and thunder did not fall silent there.

People named those lands the Storm Grove.
book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_18: Kitay Bahsi did not keep the ore he discovered to himself. He taught other smiths how to melt it, cast it, and work it.
book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_19:
After the master's death, the smiths gathered together.

They wanted future generations to know the metal he had discovered. Inspired by their master's name, they called it Kiday.
book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_20: Centuries passed. Kingdoms fell and cities sank into the earth. Nothing remained of Kitay Bahsi's forge.
book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_21: Yet the ore still lay deep within the mountains, and Lei Gong's avatars still wandered among the storms.
book.create_kiday.chronicle.page_22:
A saying left by the old smiths passed from generation to generation:

Iron carries force; Kiday remembers force.
create_kiday.ponder.production_line.text: 1. Raw Kiday becomes 144 mB Molten Kiday in a heated Basin with a Mixer at 32 RPM or faster. Superheat is not required.
2. The Pattern is visible on top. The table is not a storage tank; it accepts only the exact amount required by the installed Pattern.
3. The output is still an uncooled Molten casting. Every Molten product has its own silhouette and texture.
4. The last left-to-right step is Bulk Washing: a fan blows through water and cools the Molten casting into a usable part.
create_kiday.ponder.patterns.text_1: Place a Blank Pattern and its sample under a powered Deployer. The sample is consumed and a distinctly marked Pattern is produced.
create_kiday.ponder.lightning_engine.tex: 1. The custom copper rod attracts lightning and charges the engine for a limited time.
2. Kinetic power leaves through the visible Create shaft on the front face.
3. Look at the back-centered Create value box and scroll to select 1–64 RPM.
